summary: feat(sync): fill the temporal-filter mapping so --since and the stored watermark send lastModifiedGe (issue #13)
reason: sync --since and the stored last_synced_at watermark were both inert: the generated syncResourceSinceParam / syncResourceSinceParamFormat switches were EMPTY (the printer only emits them from an x-pp-sync-since hint the Fiken spec does not carry), so both walkers hit the 'endpoint declares no temporal filter' branch for every resource, dropped the window, emitted sync_warning reason=resource_not_incremental and re-pulled every page of every resource for every company on every run - about 1500 sequential requests for the four-company mirror behind a one-request flock (issue #13). The API does support it: spec.yaml declares the shared components.parameters.lastModifiedGe (type string, format date, YYYY-MM-DD, INCLUSIVE) on exactly five of the synced list operations - getContacts (:718), getJournalEntries (:1131), getTransactions (:1274), getProducts (:2770), getSales (:2914) - and the payloads carry a matching lastModifiedDate. (getInvoices :1381, getCreditNotes :1815 and getTimeEntries :4082 declare it too but are not sync resources.) purchases declares no filter and carries no lastModifiedDate; accounts, bank_accounts, companies, inbox and projects declare no date filter at all. Those five keep the resource_not_incremental warning and a full pull, unchanged and asserted. THE MAPPING goes into the generated switches, not into the hand-authored resolver seam, because the pair IS the printed data table for this: a reprint that ever learns the parameter should collide with it in the diff rather than silently disagree with a mapping hidden elsewhere. Both arms are marked PATCH(sync-since-last-modified) and the seams syncSinceParamFor / syncSinceParamFormatFor still delegate to them. THE VALUE is not the raw watermark. lastModifiedGe compares a DAY, so a time-of-day suffix is not a valid value at all, and the day it compares against carries no zone. syncSinceWindowValue (internal/cli/sync_since.go) therefore floors the value to its day (formatSyncSinceValue's existing 'date' arm) and then steps back ONE day. The floor is forced by the format; the extra day is the margin the day granularity costs - the client's local day boundary is not the one the API stamped the row with, the watermark is written when a run ENDS while rows keep changing during it, and client and server clocks need not agree. Cost: at most two days of rows re-upserted per incremental run, which is idempotent; the failure it prevents (a row modified during the run, never seen again) is permanent. A format this function does not understand is passed through unchanged, so a future timestamp filter is not silently widened. It is applied at the single formatting site in each walker, so --since and the watermark path get the same treatment. THE WINDOW IS A VALUE, not a bare flag: windowedPull / depWindowedPull are now syncPullWindow {Param, Value, Windowed} built by newSyncPullWindow, the request reads Param/Value, shouldRecordResultCount reads Windowed (a windowed pull gets the FILTERED Fiken-Api-Result-Count back and must never overwrite the full-collection number recorded beside sync_state.total_count - issue #15's reason for the flag, now reachable in production rather than only from a test), and AllowsDeletion() is the contract issue #17's deletion pass must consult: a pull that asked for the rows changed since a date cannot conclude that an absent row is gone. The per-pull result_count_mismatch comparison still runs for a windowed pull, because header and rows describe the same filtered set. OUT OF SCOPE, deliberately: no cursor or watermark persistence changes. --since is a window the caller supplies, which is how nOracle drives it; the issue's 'related gap' (sync_state keyed by resource_type alone, so the watermark is mirror-wide rather than per (company, resource), and a dependent sync interrupted at company 3 of 4 restarts at company 1 page 0) is a separate change and stays open. Until it lands, the automatic watermark path is only correct for a single-company mirror or a full re-pull; --since and --full are the controls a multi-company caller should use. USER-FACING NOTE (the README/SKILL line is deferred to the orchestrator, which holds those files): `fiken-cli sync --since 7d` now really does ask Fiken for only what changed, for contacts, journal_entries, transactions, products and sales - the window is sent as lastModifiedGe with the start day floored and moved back one day, so a run re-pulls a day or two of already-seen rows rather than risk missing one. accounts, bank_accounts, companies, inbox, projects and purchases have no date filter on their Fiken endpoints: they are still pulled in full and each says so once with reason=resource_not_incremental. An incremental run deliberately does not update the recorded result_count, because the API's count describes the window, not the collection.

windowedPull := newSyncPullWindow(sinceParam, effectiveSince, userParams, resource, false)
depWindowedPull := newSyncPullWindow(depSinceParam, depSinceTS, userParams, dep.Name, true)
validated_outcome: make check green (go vet ./..., go test ./..., scripts/check-boundaries.sh) plus go test -race ./internal/cli/.... Hand-authored tests in internal/cli/sync_since_test.go, on the httptest rowServer/pageServer harness: TestSyncResourceSinceParam_MapsOnlyTheFilteredResources pins the data table both ways (five resources map to lastModifiedGe/date, the other six to "" - sending a synthetic parameter to them would be a 400); TestSyncSinceWindowValue_FloorsToDayAndStepsBackOne pins the value rule including month and year boundaries and the two pass-through cases; TestSyncPullWindow_WindowedPullForbidsDeletion pins the issue #17 contract, including a --resource-param pull that is windowed with no since value; TestSyncDependentResource_SinceSendsDayFlooredLastModifiedGe drives a real --since 7d contacts pull and asserts lastModifiedGe equals (now-7d floored, minus one) on every request with no other date parameter and no warning; TestSyncDependentResource_UnmappedResourceStillWarnsNotIncremental asserts accounts sends no date parameter and emits exactly one resource_not_incremental naming itself; TestSyncDependentResource_WindowedPullKeepsRecordedResultCount asserts a windowed short pull still emits one result_count_mismatch while the recorded 577 survives; TestSyncResource_WatermarkSendsWindowedLastModifiedGe drives the automatic path (sync_state last_synced_at set, no --since) through the resolver seams and asserts the derived window, and that --full sends none. Every new test was checked red against the pre-fix code (empty switch, and separately without the minus-one-day step). The existing TestSyncResource_WindowedPullKeepsRecordedResultCount and TestSyncResource_ResourceParamPullKeepsRecordedResultCount still pass unchanged. No live API call was made and no fiken write command was run.
